Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities,

IS : 8751 ( Part II ) - 1978 

Indian Standard 

FOOTWEAR SIZES IN MONDOPOINT SYSTEM 

PART II LENGTH GRADING 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part II ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 8 June 1978, after the draft finalized by the 
Footwear Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical 
Division Council. 

0.2 The existing system of footwear sizes followed in India is known as 
English size scale and is covered in IS : 1638-1969*. It is expected that 
in the near future, a changeover to the internationally accepted Mondo- 
point system will take place progressively. The fundamental characteri- 
stics of the Mondopoint system are given in IS : 8751 ( Part I )-1978f, 
and that standard is expected to familiarize footwear manufacturers, 
traders and users with the basic features of the Mondopoint system. In 
this part of the standard, length gradings are laid down. Width gradings 
are expected to be finalized in the near future. 

0.3 This standard is based on ISO 3355-1975 Shoe sizes — System of 
length grading ( for use in the Mondopoint system ), published by the 
International Organization for Standardization. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part II ) prescribes the system of grading of lengths 
for use in the Mondopoint system of footwear sizes. The length gradings 
are applicable to all types of footwear. 

2. TERMINOLOGY 

2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 2050- 
1967+ and IS : 8751 ( Part I )-1978f shall apply. 



*Sizes and fittings of footwear {first revision ). 

tFootwear sizes in Mondopoint system: Part I Fundamental characteristics. 

^Glossary of footwear terms. 



IS : 8751 ( Part II ) - 1978 

3. LENGTH INTERVALS 

3.1 Length intervals upon which the Mondopoint system is based shaii 
be 5 mm or 7*5 mm, the origin of the grade being fixed at zero, h is 
expected that for most footwear, the length intervals of 5 mm shall be 
adequate. However, in special situations, the interval of 7*5 mm may 
be necessary. 

4. METHOD OF INDICATING THE LENGTH 

4.1 Indication of length in the size marking shall always be given in 
millimetres. In the series of lengths with interval of 7 S 5 mm, the 
indication of length in size marking shall be to the nearest lower whole 
number. 

5. LENGTHS 

5.1 Table 1 specifies, as an illustration, all lengths between 105 and 
300 mm, for use in Mondopoint system. 



IS : 8751 ( Part II ) - 1978
